architecture.mechanism: Optical stimulation of replacement motor neurons creates a control interface that selectively restores function to targeted muscles when the native neuromuscular pathway fails.
architecture.intervention: Add a photonic position-encoding channel (LED/photodiode pair) to the shifter electrical assembly that reports shift position to the steering/brake interlock logic in parallel with the chattering electrical contact path, so the safety-critical interlock no longer depends on the intermittent contact.
architecture.expected_effect: Because the optical channel is immune to contact bounce and EMI, the intermittent buzzing can no longer drop the interlock signals, so steering and brake control remain available while the fault is logged for the dealer instead of being non-duplicable.
architecture.falsification_test: Reproduce the buzzing on a bench by injecting intermittent contact resistance across the shifter contacts for 100k cycles while logging both the electrical and optical position channels; if the optical channel ever drops out or the steering/brake interlock is lost during chatter, the mechanism is falsified.
